Simulate data from a fitted multispecies model

Source: R/fp_occu_ms-outputs.R
simulate.fp_occu_ms.Rd

Generates new detections from an fp_occu_ms() fit, keeping the structure of the original data (sites, occasions and their covariates, recorders, which occasions were verified or checked), as simulate.fp_occu() does for one species. In development, as fp_occu_ms().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_ms'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, truth = c("mean", "posterior"), ...)

Arguments

object

An fp_occu_ms object.

nsim

Number of datasets.

seed

Optional integer seed.

truth

Parameter values to simulate from: "mean" (default) uses the posterior means for every dataset; "posterior" uses a different random posterior draw for each dataset, which carries the uncertainty of the fit into the simulations.

...

Unused.

Value

A list of nsim elements, each a list with data (an fp_data object with the structure and the species column of the original data) and truth: pars, the generating values of each species named as in simulate.fp_occu() with the species in brackets (occ_x[species], det_(Intercept)[species], fp_(Intercept)[species], ...); z, the latent states, a matrix of sites by species; p10_site, the false-positive rate of each site and species, a matrix of the same shape; and p10_bar, its mean over sites for each species. All the species of a dataset take their values from the same posterior draw (or from the posterior means).

See also

fp_occu_ms(), simulate_fp_ms()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
s <- simulate_fp_ms(nspecies = 4, nsite = 60, seed = 1)
m <- fp_occu_ms(s$data, occ = ~ x, det = ~ bio, random_recorder = FALSE)
new <- simulate(m, nsim = 2, seed = 1)
new[[1]]$truth$pars
} # }
